clue.text: See 11
Titanic accepting disaster finally, as ship

indicators.note: the word for huge takes another letter into its middle

parts.note: titanic means huge, so big

indicators.note: only the closing letter of disaster is wanted

explanation.surface: A sentence about the doomed liner Titanic taking on disaster as a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Titanic' looks like the famous liner, but it is just an adjective meaning huge.
explanation.definitionFit: A brig is a two-masted square-rigged sailing vessel, a kind of ship.

clue.text: Following doctor out, incense passed round

indicators.note: the word for anger is wrapped around the rearranged letters

parts.note: to incense someone is to make them furious, to enrage them

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of out get rearranged

explanation.surface: A church scene: after the doctor leaves, incense is passed round the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' is a noun here, a retinue, not a preposition; 'doctor' is the anagram signal, not a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: A following is a group of attendants or supporters, which is what an entourage is.

clue.text: Harbour on Guernsey, perhaps, set up for a global line

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means the letters are read upwards, so backwards
the harbour word follows the island abbreviation

parts.note: Guernsey is one of the Channel Islands, abbreviated CI
a harbour is a port

explanation.surface: A harbour on Guernsey being constructed for a shipping route around the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' means placed after the island abbreviation, and 'set up' reverses the lot, as down entries read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are lines of latitude drawn around the globe.

clue.text: Girl's a sucker for the director

parts.note: Joy is a girl's name, with the possessive S
a tick is a bloodsucking parasite

explanation.surface: A girl is said to be a soft touch for the film director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sucker' reads as a gullible person, but here it is a bloodsucking insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A control stick steers an aircraft or game, so it directs where things go.

clue.text: Going under vehicle, the Queen's an original American character — that's not on! Good Lord!

indicators.note: in a down entry the rest of the pieces go beneath the vehicle

parts.note: a jeep is a rugged vehicle
ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the Queen, plus the possessive S
the Cree are a Native American people, original inhabitants

indicators.note: the letters o and n are removed from the word for character

parts.note: a character in a story is a person

explanation.surface: A mechanic sliding under a vehicle meets a strange American figure and exclaims in outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's not on!' looks like an exclamation of disapproval, but it tells you to drop ON from PERSON, leaving PERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild American exclamations of surprise, euphemisms for the name of Jesus.

clue.text: Easy to mix part of a cake that's more frothy

indicators.note: mixing scrambles the letters of easy

parts.note: a wedding cake is built in tiers

explanation.surface: Baking instructions: an easy layer of cake that ends up fluffier.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast makes things froth, so something yeastier is frothier, comparative form matching.

clue.text: For example, dip one in the fire, primarily

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the following letters

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: only the first letter of fire is used

explanation.surface: Someone dipping a single item into the fire, perhaps a log or toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dip' is old slang for a pickpocket, so it is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dip is a pickpocket, one kind of stealer, hence an example of a robber.

clue.text: Deformity in giant clone is innate

indicators.note: the letters of the next words are bent out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A genetics report: a misshapen feature in an enormous clone is inborn.
explanation.definitionFit: Congenital conditions are present from birth, which is what innate means.

clue.text: See 13
13 9 beings oddly covered up?

parts.note: 13-across is Area, shortened to its initial
9-across is fifty-one, which in Roman numerals is LI

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of beings are hidden, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Creatures at the famous Nevada base, mysteriously hushed up by the authorities?
explanation.walkthrough: Area 51 is a secret US Air Force base in Nevada linked to UFO conspiracy theories. 'oddly covered up' hides B, I, G and leaves E, N, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Conspiracy theorists claim the base houses extraterrestrial creatures from crashed spacecraft.

clue.text: Mysterious affair seen briefly coming over in profundity?

definitions.text: Mysterious affair seen briefly coming over in profundity?

parts.words: Mysterious affair seen briefly coming over in profundity?
parts.note: the abbreviation of the full phrase is a sighting of an unknown craft, and its three letters appear backwards inside the word profundity

explanation.surface: A puzzling event glimpsed fleetingly in some deep meditation.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse can only show the clue as a whole: 'seen briefly' points to the abbreviation UFO, and 'coming over in' says those letters lie reversed in prOFUndity.
explanation.definitionFit: A mysterious sky sighting nobody can explain is the classic flying saucer report.

clue.text: Agreeable chap put on coat for builder

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece is placed on top of the second

parts.note: a brick is old slang for a good, dependable fellow
a coat of paint is a layer

explanation.surface: A pleasant fellow putting on his coat before heading off to the building site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brick' as a dependable, good-natured person is dated British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A bricklayer is a tradesman who constructs walls, so a builder.

clue.text: Mysterious affair, yeti? Mysterious place

indicators.note: something mysterious is puzzling and jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, but its I is the Roman numeral for one, so it counts as YET plus ONE

explanation.surface: A mysterious business involving an abominable snowman, in a mysterious spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mysterious' rearranges AFFAIR YETI into AREA FIFTY I; the leftover I is the Roman numeral for one, giving the base usually written Area 51.
explanation.definitionFit: Area 51 is a secretive US Air Force site in Nevada famous for conspiracy theories.

clue.text: Border dropped in scheme before old country backs plot

indicators.note: the first piece comes ahead of the second
the border word is removed from inside the word scheme

parts.note: a hem is a border of cloth

indicators.note: the old country pair is read backwards

parts.note: Iran is a country

explanation.surface: A political plot: a border plan dropped before an ancient nation supports the conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped in' takes HEM out of SCHEME, leaving SCE; 'backs' turns O IRAN into NARIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is the outline of a story's events, which is a plot.

clue.text: Vital channel confiscates evil weapons

indicators.note: the vessel word seizes and holds another word inside it

parts.note: an artery is a vital blood vessel, also a main route
ill can mean evil, as in ill will

explanation.surface: A key TV channel seizing nasty weaponry, perhaps in a news story about arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'channel' suggests television, but a vital channel is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery is large-calibre guns, a collective term for heavy armaments.

clue.text: That's my emerald, originally shaped as a gem

indicators.note: shaping the letters reforms them in a new order
only the initial of emerald is used

explanation.surface: A jeweller proudly showing off an emerald, cut to look like another stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Amethyst is a purple variety of quartz prized as a precious stone.

clue.text: Baby an attention grabber in the newspapers?

definitions.meaning: a bawling infant who cries loudly

definitions.text: an attention grabber in the newspapers?
definitions.meaning: a sensational headline in large type, also called a banner

explanation.surface: A tabloid splash about an infant that is designed to catch the reader's eye.
explanation.definitionFit: One who yells is a bawling infant; in journalism the word also names a sensational headline.

clue.text: Loathsome thing being transported like a caravan, did you say?

indicators.note: the word is heard as spoken, sounding like another

parts.note: a caravan is pulled behind a car, so it is towed

explanation.surface: A grumbler calls a holiday caravan being hauled along a loathsome thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Toad is used figuratively for a repulsive, contemptible person or creature.

clue.text: Service industry finally heads for the hills?

parts.note: Mass is a church service

indicators.note: the first letters of the following two words are taken

explanation.surface: The service industry finally escapes to the countryside for a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service industry' reads as one phrase, but Service is a church Mass and industry gives just its I.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains, a mass of high ground.

clue.text: Observer who's not seen to turn left, left and left again, anyhow

indicators.note: turning the letters around reorders them

parts.note: L again is the abbreviation for left
L again is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Directions for a confused stalker told to keep turning left.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'left' is used in full; the next two are just L; 'and' and 'again' are joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly on the wall watches events unnoticed, an unseen witness to private scenes.

clue.text: Drunk not making a squeak?

definitions.meaning: a hinge treated with lubricant no longer squeaks

explanation.definitionFit: Well-lubricated machinery is silent, and well-oiled is slang for drunk.

clue.text: Slice of meat cut for pastry dish

indicators.note: cut means the end is chopped off

parts.note: flank is a cut of beef

explanation.surface: A butcher trimming meat to put into a pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like part of the meat description but tells you to trim the final K from FLANK.
explanation.definitionFit: A flan is an open pastry case with a sweet or savoury filling, like a tart.

clue.text: Secondary action attributed to freedom of movement

parts.note: by indicates authorship, as in a book by an author
play is slack or room to move in a mechanism

explanation.surface: A legal or theatrical note about who is responsible for a side event.
explanation.definitionFit: Byplay is subsidiary stage action going on alongside the main scene.

clue.text: Wind describing a festival?

definitions.meaning: a breeze blowing from the east
an adverb formed from the spring festival name, a mock word for in a festive spring manner

explanation.definitionFit: A wind from the east is named after its direction; split, it looks like an adverb from the spring holiday.

clue.text: Raw food cursed, it needing to be cooked

indicators.note: cooking the letters means mixing them up

explanation.surface: A chef swearing about a dish that has to be cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: The paradox is the joke: raw food that needs cooking, but only its letters are cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Crudites are raw vegetable sticks served as a starter with dips.

clue.text: See 11
